descriptionChirho: The institution of marriage or the celebratory wedding feast and banquet associated with it. All occurrences across grammatical cases (nominative, accusative, genitive, plural and singular) refer uniformly to the same concept. Spanish consistently uses 'bodas/boda' and 'banquete'; Hindi uses 'विवाह' (vivah) and 'विवाह-भोज' (wedding feast); Arabic uses 'العُرسِ/عُرْسُ' (al-urs); Korean uses '혼인 잔치' (honin janchi, wedding feast) and '혼인' (honin, marriage); Swahili uses 'arusi/harusi/ndoa'. The semantic range spans both the ceremony itself and the accompanying feast, a natural polysemy within a single lexical sense rather than distinct meanings.
